attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: A causal claim that CUDA's lead produces a functional monopoly. Limiting it to AI GPUs follows from the surrounding text. The 'in theory, competition' caveat is dropped, but the meaning is unchanged.

contract.note: Reading 'functional monopoly' as entrenched practical dominance is fair and ordinary. Not requiring CUDA to be the sole cause is fair too. The result depends on unstated thresholds for dominance and for CUDA's share of the cause.

evidence.note: Omdia, Aug 2025: NVIDIA is the dominant vendor, but alternatives and AMD are gaining. It covers the wider accelerator market, gives no AI GPU share, and does not measure CUDA's causal role.
Gaudi-2 versus A100 study: competitive hardware, weaker software maturity. One alternative and a narrow setting, so it cannot show market dominance or ecosystem parity.
French competition authority, June 2024: alternatives to CUDA are emerging. Too early to measure the late-2025 position.

reviews.rationale: The packet points to NVIDIA dominance and a CUDA software lead, but nothing measures the AI GPU market share in late 2025 or shows how much CUDA sustains that position. Alternatives are reported as gaining ground. Neither the support condition nor the contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his post.

semantics.note: A bundle of five present-tense empirical assertions, faithfully restated. 'Pipedream' is folded into 'do not work', which is acceptable.

contract.note: Reading the agent claim as a categorical denial follows the words 'simply do not work'. Measuring inference cost at comparable performance is one ordinary reading. Provider cost or total spend could change that part, and the contract flags this.

evidence.note: METR randomized trial: experienced open-source developers were 19% slower with AI in early 2025. Supports slowdown in that one setting only.
METR, March 2025: frontier agents have a 50% time horizon of about 50 minutes on multi-step tasks. This contradicts the categorical 'do not work', though reliability limits remain.
Through Nov 2025, the price for a given performance level falls exponentially, even at benchmark level after counting extra tokens. This contradicts the reading that unit cost keeps rising.
METR follow-up published Feb 2026: weak, selection-biased signs of speedup. Its window is not isolated to before the post, so it is context only.

reviews.rationale: Supported: developer slowdown in one controlled setting, and models having real limits. Contradicted: agents 'simply do not work', since agents repeatedly succeed on bounded tasks, and rising inference cost, since comparable-performance prices fell. 'Unreliable' and a general slowdown are not shown across the board.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words. Nadella's quote is quoted support, not the claim itself.

semantics.note: A present-state claim of insufficient built, powered capacity for the six million Blackwell GPUs. Faithfully restated.

contract.note: Requiring compatible, commissioned, powered capacity matched against the shipment cohort is an ordinary reading. Counting units (dies vs packages) and per-GPU power assumptions materially affect the result.

evidence.note: Nadella, Oct 2025: Microsoft lacks warm shells for some chips. A real constraint at one company, with no Blackwell-wide quantification.
CBRE, H1 2025: record-low 1.6% vacancy in North America. Regional and earlier than the target month, and not Blackwell-compatible capacity.
Published Apr 2026, before the evaluation date. Reads six million as dies, about 3 million packages. That undercuts the post's power arithmetic but does not show capacity was sufficient.

reviews.rationale: No inventory of compatible, powered capacity for November 2025 and no verified power requirement for the cohort are in the packet. Constraints at one firm and regional vacancy figures show the market was tight, but they cannot establish or refute a shortfall for the whole cohort.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: The core factual claim is NVIDIA's outsized market weight. Setting aside the 'only reason you're hearing about it' aside is reasonable.

contract.note: Reading the metaphor as unusually large influence on index weight and returns is fair and ordinary. It does not stretch the claim into a collapse claim.

evidence.note: Reuters, 14 Nov 2025: NVIDIA held about 8% of the S&P 500 and about 10% of the Nasdaq 100, and its moves can sway indexes. A dated weight inside the target month.

reviews.rationale: Dated November 2025 reporting gives NVIDIA about 8% of the S&P 500 and 10% of the Nasdaq 100, enough to sway broad indexes. That meets the support condition on the plain reading of 'load-bearing'.
